title: Depreciation of buildings: recovery period, method and convention
rule: Under the general depreciation system, a building that is residential rental property is recovered over 27.5 years and one that is nonresidential real property over 39 years, both by the straight line method with salvage value treated as zero. Both use the mid-month convention: a building placed in service or disposed of during a month is treated as placed in service or disposed of at the midpoint of that month. A building is residential rental property if 80 percent or more of its gross rental income for the year comes from dwelling units. Land is not depreciable, so only the cost allocated to the building and other improvements is recovered.
changeWatch: Amendments to the recovery periods in section 168(c) or the real property convention in 168(d)(2); the IRS reissues Publication 946 each year (the 2025 edition, last updated April 30, 2026, was current on 2026-11-13).
